page: Amazon Web Services t3.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the t3.xlarge in the lower performance tiers, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU metrics falling into the bottom 25 percent. Memory bandwidth tests show 167.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 23.93 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance exhibits modest performance in high-throughput tasks, as evidenced by a static web serving throughput of 2.74 GB/sec and low LLM inference speeds on small models. These results reflect the burstable CPU allocation model, which is designed for workloads with transient spikes rather than sustained high-utilization compute.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t3.xlarge offers a budget-friendly profile for workloads with low average CPU utilization. It is suited for general-purpose applications such as development environments, code repositories, low-traffic web servers, and small database instances that benefit from burstable performance without the cost of dedicated, continuously high-compute resources.
